errors: First variogram test expected Brownian-bridge variance t(1-t)L; gamma(h)=h is BM with increment variance 2h, so 2t(1-t)L; test fixed, engine was right.
CSV exporter first lacked the formula-injection guard; check_csv_formula_guard.py caught it in preflight; guard and test added.

doc_friction.issue: Asks that each paper's DOI be checked; api.crossref.org, USGS, NOAA and EPA hosts were all refused by this session's proxy, so DOIs went in unchecked (said so in README) and no new real dataset could be downloaded; reused ERA5 data already in research/marine-hull.

pip install of a reference package (pykrige) was refused by the auto-mode classifier; independent references had to be built from closed-form results and a separate Cholesky solver instead. Worth noting that third-party reference packages may be unavailable.

notes: Explore idea: kriging as a research-algorithm tool (ventures/kriging-interpolation); no venture README mentioned kriging or variograms. Ordinary kriging (Matheron 1963), Matheron and Cressie-Hawkins semivariograms, Cressie 1985 WLS fit (spherical/exponential/gaussian), Dubrule 1983 closed-form LOO, IDW and nearest baselines, lon/lat by chordal distance (Gneiting 2013). Real example: ERA5 Jan 2024 median Hs at 371 ocean points: LOO RMSE kriging 0.390 m, nearest 0.505, IDW 0.623. Simulation (40 known fields, 4,000 held-out sites): 95% coverage 95.1%, MSDR 1.00, kriging beat IDW on 36/40. 38 tests. Next: anisotropy, universal kriging. No agent doc: the README and the run record carry what the next run needs.
